blocks.en: The Empty Tomb
blocks.es_reference: El Sepulcro Vacío

blocks.en: The tomb was sealed and the guard was set, but the last word had not been spoken. As the first day of the week began to dawn, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb. There was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended, rolled back the stone, and sat on it, his countenance like lightning and his clothing white as snow. The guards shook and became like dead men. The angel said to the women, "Do not be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus who was crucified. He is not here; for He is risen, as He said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay" (Matthew 28:5-6). The stone was not rolled away to let Jesus out, for He was already risen; it was rolled away to let the witnesses in. The same women who had watched Him die and seen where He was buried now stood in an empty tomb.
blocks.es_reference: El sepulcro estaba sellado y la guardia puesta, pero la última palabra no se había dicho. Al amanecer del primer día de la semana, María Magdalena y la otra María vinieron a ver el sepulcro. Hubo un gran terremoto, porque un ángel del Señor descendió, removió la piedra, y se sentó sobre ella, su rostro como un relámpago y su vestidura blanca como la nieve. Los guardias temblaron y quedaron como muertos. El ángel dijo a las mujeres: "No temáis; porque yo sé que buscáis a Jesús, el que fue crucificado. No está aquí; pues ha resucitado, como dijo. Venid, ved el lugar donde fue puesto el Señor" (Mateo 28:5-6). La piedra no fue removida para dejar salir a Jesús, porque ya había resucitado; fue removida para dejar entrar a los testigos. Las mismas mujeres que le habían visto morir y habían visto dónde fue sepultado ahora estaban de pie en un sepulcro vacío.

blocks.en: He Is Risen
blocks.es_reference: Ha Resucitado

blocks.en: The women departed quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, and ran to bring His disciples word. And as they went, Jesus Himself met them, saying, "Rejoice!" They came and held Him by the feet and worshiped Him. He told them not to be afraid, but to go and tell His brethren to go to Galilee, where they would see Him. The message of Easter is that the resurrection changes lives, and it begins to change them in that very moment: the grief of Friday becomes the joy of Sunday. Over the next forty days He appeared again and again, and Paul records that on one occasion more than five hundred saw Him at once, many of whom were still living and could be asked. This is no tissue of fable; it is the best-attested event of the ancient world.
blocks.es_reference: Las mujeres salieron aprisa del sepulcro con temor y gran gozo, y corrieron a dar las nuevas a los discípulos. Y mientras iban, Jesús mismo les salió al encuentro, diciendo: "¡Salve!" Ellas se acercaron, abrazaron sus pies, y le adoraron. Él les dijo que no temieran, sino que fueran a decir a sus hermanos que fueran a Galilea, donde le verían. El mensaje de la Pascua es que la resurrección cambia vidas, y comienza a cambiarlas en ese mismo momento: el dolor del viernes se vuelve el gozo del domingo. Durante los siguientes cuarenta días apareció una y otra vez, y Pablo registra que en una ocasión más de quinientos le vieron a la vez, muchos de los cuales aún vivían y podían ser interrogados. Esto no es una fábula; es el suceso mejor atestiguado del mundo antiguo.

blocks.en: The Guards and the Lie
blocks.es_reference: Los Guardias y la Mentira

blocks.en: While the women ran with the truth, some of the guard came into the city and reported to the chief priests everything that had happened. The leaders assembled, took counsel, and gave the soldiers a large sum of money, telling them to say that His disciples came by night and stole Him while they slept. So they took the money and did as they were instructed, and that saying was spread among the Jews. It is a strange testimony: the enemies of Jesus did not deny that the tomb was empty. They could not produce a body. They could only invent a story, and a poor one, for sleeping men make poor witnesses to a theft they slept through. The very lie they paid for is a witness to the empty tomb they could not explain away.
blocks.es_reference: Mientras las mujeres corrían con la verdad, algunos de la guardia vinieron a la ciudad y reportaron a los principales sacerdotes todo lo que había sucedido. Los líderes se reunieron, tomaron consejo, y dieron a los soldados una gran suma de dinero, diciéndoles que dijeran que sus discípulos vinieron de noche y le robaron mientras dormían. Así que tomaron el dinero e hicieron como se les instruyó, y ese dicho se divulgó entre los judíos. Es un testimonio extraño: los enemigos de Jesús no negaron que el sepulcro estuviera vacío. No pudieron producir un cuerpo. Solo pudieron inventar una historia, y mala, porque los hombres dormidos son malos testigos de un robo que ocurrió mientras dormían. La misma mentira que pagaron es un testimonio del sepulcro vacío que no pudieron explicar.

blocks.en: The Resurrection Defeats Distress
blocks.es_reference: La Resurrección Vence la Angustia

blocks.en: The women came to the tomb in deep grief, carrying spices to do one last service for the Lord they loved, and they left it running with great joy. The resurrection turns sorrow into joy because it answers our deepest distress, which is death itself. My first encounter with family grief came when I was about fourteen. I had a little niece, a beautiful baby, born with fluid on the brain; I remember pressing the small tube in her neck that drained it. When she was about a year and a half she needed another operation, and something went wrong, and she died. I remember my mother on the drive home from the hospital throwing her arms around me and crying, "Why did God let our baby die?" I had no answer then, and after years of study I still have no full answer to that question. But I believe with all my heart that I will see her again, because the tomb is empty and Christ is risen. That is what the resurrection does to our distress: it does not pretend the grave is nothing, but it promises that the grave is not the end.
blocks.es_reference: Las mujeres vinieron al sepulcro en profundo dolor, llevando especias para hacer un último servicio al Señor que amaban, y salieron de él corriendo con gran gozo. La resurrección convierte la tristeza en gozo porque responde a nuestra angustia más profunda, que es la muerte misma. Mi primer encuentro con el dolor familiar vino cuando tenía unos catorce años. Tenía una sobrinita, una bebé hermosa, nacida con líquido en el cerebro; recuerdo presionar el pequeño tubo en su cuello que lo drenaba. Cuando tenía como año y medio necesitó otra operación, y algo salió mal, y murió. Recuerdo a mi madre en el camino de regreso del hospital echando sus brazos a mi alrededor y llorando: "¿Por qué dejó Dios morir a nuestra bebé?" No tuve respuesta entonces, y después de años de estudio todavía no tengo una respuesta completa a esa pregunta. Pero creo con todo mi corazón que la veré otra vez, porque el sepulcro está vacío y Cristo ha resucitado. Eso es lo que la resurrección hace con nuestra angustia: no finge que la tumba no es nada, pero promete que la tumba no es el fin.

blocks.en: The Resurrection Defeats Doubt
blocks.es_reference: La Resurrección Vence la Duda

blocks.en: When Jesus first appeared in the upper room, the disciples believed, but Thomas was not there, and he would not take their word for it. He said he would not believe unless he saw the nail scars and put his finger where the nails had been, for he knew that dead men do not rise. A week later Jesus appeared again, and this time Thomas was present, and the Lord showed him His hands and His side. Thomas answered, "My Lord and my God!" (John 20:28). I will be honest with you: I have had doubts. I have doubted whether there is a God, doubted whether Christianity is true, doubted whether God answers prayer, doubted His love, and doubted whether I had the gifts to preach. In the end it is the resurrection that conquers my doubts, for if Christ is risen then God is real, the gospel is true, and death is defeated. The Lord did not rebuke Thomas for needing to see; He met him in his doubt and turned it into worship.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando Jesús apareció por primera vez en el aposento alto, los discípulos creyeron, pero Tomás no estaba allí, y no tomó su palabra. Dijo que no creería a menos que viera las marcas de los clavos y pusiera su dedo donde habían estado los clavos, porque sabía que los muertos no resucitan. Una semana después Jesús apareció otra vez, y esta vez Tomás estaba presente, y el Señor le mostró sus manos y su costado. Tomás respondió: "¡Señor mío, y Dios mío!" (Juan 20:28). Seré honesto con ustedes: he tenido dudas. He dudado si hay un Dios, dudado si el cristianismo es verdad, dudado si Dios responde la oración, dudado de su amor, y dudado si tenía los dones para predicar. Al final es la resurrección la que vence mis dudas, porque si Cristo ha resucitado entonces Dios es real, el evangelio es verdad, y la muerte está vencida. El Señor no reprendió a Tomás por necesitar ver; le encontró en su duda y la convirtió en adoración.

blocks.en: The Resurrection Defeats Denial
blocks.es_reference: La Resurrección Vence la Negación

blocks.en: Peter had sworn that though all others fell away he never would, and within hours he denied his Lord three times, the last time with cursing, saying he did not even know the man. But Jesus did not leave Peter to drown in his guilt. On the seashore the risen Lord asked him three times, "Do you love Me?" — one question for each denial — and three times He gave him back his calling: "Feed My sheep" (John 21:17). And the Peter who had denied Christ in a courtyard stood up on the day of Pentecost and preached Him boldly in the open street. I must confess that I too have denied Christ, not as Peter did, but in the subtler way of silence; there have been times God gave me an opening and I said nothing. The resurrection answers that failure, for the same Lord who restored Peter restores us, and the Spirit who emboldened a denier can embolden us to speak.
blocks.es_reference: Pedro había jurado que aunque todos los demás cayeran él nunca lo haría, y en pocas horas negó a su Señor tres veces, la última con maldiciones, diciendo que ni siquiera conocía al hombre. Pero Jesús no dejó a Pedro ahogarse en su culpa. En la orilla del mar el Señor resucitado le preguntó tres veces: "¿Me amas?" — una pregunta por cada negación — y tres veces le devolvió su llamado: "Apacienta mis ovejas" (Juan 21:17). Y el Pedro que había negado a Cristo en un patio se levantó en el día de Pentecostés y le predicó con denuedo en la calle abierta. Debo confesar que yo también he negado a Cristo, no como Pedro, sino en la manera más sutil del silencio; ha habido veces en que Dios me dio una oportunidad y no dije nada. La resurrección responde a esa falta, porque el mismo Señor que restauró a Pedro nos restaura, y el Espíritu que dio valor a un negador puede darnos valor para hablar.

blocks.en: The Resurrection Defeats Disgust
blocks.es_reference: La Resurrección Vence el Rechazo

blocks.en: Saul of Tarsus was a man filled with hatred for the church, going from house to house to drag off believers and put them in prison. On the road to Damascus a light from heaven flashed around him, and he fell and heard a voice say, "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?" When he asked who it was, the answer came, "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting" (Acts 9:4-5). The encounter with the risen Christ so transformed him that the great persecutor became the great missionary, and the man who had hunted Christians spent his life proclaiming Christ. The resurrection can break even a heart set in hatred or turned away in bitterness, for the living Lord still meets people on their road and turns their disgust into worship.
blocks.es_reference: Saulo de Tarso era un hombre lleno de odio hacia la iglesia, yendo de casa en casa para arrastrar a los creyentes y meterlos en prisión. En el camino a Damasco una luz del cielo resplandeció alrededor de él, y cayó y oyó una voz que decía: "Saulo, Saulo, ¿por qué me persigues?" Cuando preguntó quién era, vino la respuesta: "Yo soy Jesús, a quien tú persigues" (Hechos 9:4-5). El encuentro con el Cristo resucitado lo transformó de tal manera que el gran perseguidor llegó a ser el gran misionero, y el hombre que había cazado cristianos pasó su vida proclamando a Cristo. La resurrección puede quebrar aun un corazón fijado en el odio o vuelto en amargura, porque el Señor viviente todavía encuentra a la gente en su camino y convierte su rechazo en adoración.

blocks.en: The Great Commission
blocks.es_reference: La Gran Comisión

blocks.en: The eleven went to Galilee, to the mountain Jesus had appointed, and when they saw Him they worshiped Him, though some doubted. And Jesus came and spoke to them the words with which Matthew ends his Gospel: "All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth. Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you; and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age" (Matthew 28:18-20). The risen King claims all authority, sends His people to all nations, and commands not merely converts but disciples — baptized into the triune name and taught to obey everything He commanded. The Great Commission is not a suggestion for the gifted few but the marching order of the whole church.
blocks.es_reference: Los once fueron a Galilea, al monte que Jesús había señalado, y cuando le vieron le adoraron, aunque algunos dudaban. Y Jesús vino y les habló las palabras con las que Mateo termina su Evangelio: "Toda potestad me es dada en el cielo y en la tierra. Por tanto, id, y enseñad a todas las naciones, bautizándolas en el nombre del Padre, y del Hijo, y del Espíritu Santo; enseñándoles que guarden todas las cosas que os he mandado; y he aquí, yo estoy con vosotros todos los días, hasta el fin del mundo" (Mateo 28:18-20). El Rey resucitado reclama toda potestad, envía a su pueblo a todas las naciones, y manda no meramente convertidos sino discípulos — bautizados en el nombre trino y enseñados a obedecer todo lo que Él mandó. La Gran Comisión no es una sugerencia para unos pocos dotados sino la orden de marcha de toda la iglesia.

blocks.en: An Anatomy of Christ's Commission
blocks.es_reference: Una Anatomía de la Comisión de Cristo

blocks.en: One of the recovered Matthew sermons gives a memorable anatomy to these marching orders. The mission of Jesus makes demands on our lips, our feet, our heads, and our hearts. He puts words on our lips by giving us a message we actually believe and a method that includes both preaching and teaching: the herald does not invent the King's message, and the teacher helps believers learn all that Christ commanded. He puts movement in our feet with one word — "Go." The gospel does not merely wait for people to find it; it goes where people are. He puts a vision in our heads: "all nations" means that no race, language, people, or place lies outside the King's concern. And He puts a burden on our hearts, because those who see the world Christ sees will accept responsibility either to go or to help send those who go through prayer, identification, and material support. Matthew therefore ends not with spectators admiring a risen Christ but with disciples under orders. The King has all authority; His people have a message, a direction, a vision, and a burden.
blocks.es_reference: Uno de los sermones recuperados de Mateo da una anatomía memorable a estas órdenes de marcha. La misión de Jesús hace demandas sobre nuestros labios, nuestros pies, nuestra cabeza y nuestro corazón. Él pone palabras en nuestros labios al darnos un mensaje que realmente creemos y un método que incluye tanto predicar como enseñar: el heraldo no inventa el mensaje del Rey, y el maestro ayuda a los creyentes a aprender todo lo que Cristo mandó. Él pone movimiento en nuestros pies con una palabra: «Id». El evangelio no se limita a esperar que la gente lo encuentre; va adonde está la gente. Él pone una visión en nuestra cabeza: «todas las naciones» significa que ninguna raza, idioma, pueblo o lugar queda fuera de la preocupación del Rey. Y Él pone una carga en nuestro corazón, porque quienes ven el mundo que Cristo ve aceptarán la responsabilidad de ir o de ayudar a enviar a quienes van mediante la oración, la identificación con su ministerio y el apoyo material. Mateo, por tanto, no termina con espectadores admirando a un Cristo resucitado, sino con discípulos bajo órdenes. El Rey tiene toda autoridad; Su pueblo tiene un mensaje, una dirección, una visión y una carga.

blocks.en: God With Us, to the End
blocks.es_reference: Dios con Nosotros, hasta el Fin

blocks.en: Matthew began his Gospel by telling us that the child would be called Immanuel, which means "God with us" (Matthew 1:23), and he ends it with the risen Lord's own promise, "I am with you always, even to the end of the age." The whole book is held between those two words. The God who came to be with us in a manger, who was with us through the teaching and the miracles, who was with us even into the darkness of the cross, is now with us as the risen and reigning King, and will be with us until the age is ended. Jesus is alive. He rose from the dead, and we are His witnesses. The resurrection removes our distress, our doubt, our denial, and our disgust, and sends us out under the authority of a living King who has promised never to leave us. Every other grave in history has only footsteps leading in; the grave of Jesus has footsteps leading out, and because He lives, all who are in Christ shall live also. The Gospel that opened with a King in a manger closes with a King on a mountain, sending His people into all the world; and the same Lord who was Immanuel at the beginning walks with us still, every day, until the end of the age.
blocks.es_reference: Mateo comenzó su Evangelio diciéndonos que el niño sería llamado Emanuel, que significa "Dios con nosotros" (Mateo 1:23), y lo termina con la promesa misma del Señor resucitado: "Yo estoy con vosotros todos los días, hasta el fin del mundo." Todo el libro está sostenido entre esas dos palabras. El Dios que vino a estar con nosotros en un pesebre, que estuvo con nosotros a través de la enseñanza y los milagros, que estuvo con nosotros aun en las tinieblas de la cruz, ahora está con nosotros como el Rey resucitado y reinante, y estará con nosotros hasta que la era termine. Jesús está vivo. Resucitó de los muertos, y nosotros somos sus testigos. La resurrección quita nuestra angustia, nuestra duda, nuestra negación, y nuestro rechazo, y nos envía bajo la autoridad de un Rey viviente que ha prometido nunca dejarnos. Toda otra tumba en la historia tiene solo huellas que entran; la tumba de Jesús tiene huellas que salen, y porque Él vive, todos los que están en Cristo vivirán también. El Evangelio que abrió con un Rey en un pesebre cierra con un Rey en un monte, enviando a su pueblo a todo el mundo; y el mismo Señor que fue Emanuel al principio camina con nosotros todavía, cada día, hasta el fin de la era.

blocks.en: "Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations... and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age. Amen." — Matthew 28:19-20 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Por tanto, id, y enseñad a todas las naciones... y he aquí, yo estoy con vosotros todos los días, hasta el fin del mundo. Amén." — Mateo 28:19-20 (RVG)

mc.stem: When the women arrived at the tomb on the first day of the week, an angel:
options: Had rolled back the stone and sat on it
mc.why: His countenance was like lightning, and the guards became like dead men.

mc.stem: The angel told the women that Jesus:
options: Is not here, for He is risen, as He said
mc.why: The stone was rolled away not to let Jesus out but to let the witnesses in.

mc.stem: As the women ran from the tomb, who met them?
mc.why: They held Him by the feet and worshiped Him; their fear turned to great joy.

mc.stem: Paul records that on one occasion the risen Jesus was seen at once by:
options: More than five hundred, many still living
mc.why: The resurrection is the best-attested event of the ancient world, not a fable.

mc.stem: To explain the empty tomb, the chief priests:
options: Bribed the guards to say the disciples stole the body
mc.why: Even the enemies of Jesus could not deny the tomb was empty or produce a body.

mc.stem: The lesson notes the guards' bribed story was weak because:
options: Sleeping men make poor witnesses to a theft they slept through
mc.why: The very lie they paid for witnesses to the empty tomb they could not explain.

mc.stem: The unit frames the resurrection as defeating four things. The first is:
options: Distress — the women's grief turned to joy
mc.why: The resurrection answers our deepest distress, which is death itself.

mc.stem: When Thomas saw the risen Lord's hands and side, he said:
mc.why: The Lord met Thomas in his doubt and turned it into worship.

mc.stem: On the seashore, the risen Jesus asked Peter three times, 'Do you love Me?' and each time:
options: Gave him back his calling — 'Feed My sheep'
mc.why: One question for each denial; Jesus restored the disciple who had denied Him.

mc.stem: The persecutor whose 'disgust' was defeated when he met the risen Christ was:
options: Saul of Tarsus, on the road to Damascus
mc.why: The great persecutor became the great missionary, Paul.

mc.stem: On the road to Damascus the voice said:
options: 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?'
mc.why: 'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting' — the living Lord meets people on their road.

mc.stem: The eleven met the risen Jesus in Galilee on:
mc.why: They worshiped Him, though some doubted, and He gave the Great Commission.

mc.stem: In the Great Commission Jesus first declares that:
options: All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Him
mc.why: The command to go rests on the authority of the risen King.

mc.stem: The Great Commission commands the disciples to make disciples of:
mc.why: Baptizing in the triune name and teaching them to obey all He commanded.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, the Great Commission is:
options: The marching order of the whole church
mc.why: Not a suggestion for the gifted few but a command to all of Christ's people.

mc.stem: Jesus ends the commission with the promise:
options: 'I am with you always, even to the end of the age'
mc.why: The risen King promises His abiding presence to His sent people.

mc.stem: The lesson shows Matthew's Gospel is framed between two phrases. They are:
options: 'God with us' (1:23) and 'I am with you always' (28:20)
mc.why: The whole book is held between Immanuel and the promise of His abiding presence.

mc.stem: The lesson teaches that the God who is 'with us' was with His people:
options: From the manger through the cross to the risen reign, and to the end of the age
mc.why: The risen and reigning King has promised never to leave us.

mc.stem: The author shares that the resurrection ultimately conquered his own:
options: Doubts — and his temptation to stay silent
mc.why: If Christ is risen, God is real, the gospel is true, and death is defeated.

mc.stem: The unit concludes that, unlike every other grave, the tomb of Jesus has:
options: Footsteps leading out, because He lives
mc.why: Because He lives, all who are in Christ shall live also.

sa.prompt: Describe the scene at the empty tomb and the angel's message to the women.
sa.model: On the first day of the week Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb, and there was a great earthquake as an angel of the Lord descended, rolled back the stone, and sat on it, his face like lightning, while the guards became like dead men. The angel told the women not to be afraid, for he knew they sought Jesus who was crucified, and announced that He is not here, for He is risen, as He said, inviting them to come and see the place where the Lord lay. The stone was rolled away not to let Jesus out, since He was already risen, but to let the witnesses in. The same women who had watched Him die now stood as witnesses in an empty tomb.

sa.prompt: What happened as the women left the tomb, and how well attested is the resurrection?
sa.model: The women left the tomb with fear and great joy and ran to tell the disciples, and as they went Jesus Himself met them, saying Rejoice, and they held Him by the feet and worshiped Him. He told them not to be afraid but to send His brethren to Galilee, where they would see Him. Over the next forty days He appeared again and again, and Paul records that on one occasion more than five hundred saw Him at once, many of whom were still living and could be questioned. So the resurrection is not a fable but is well attested by many witnesses, indeed the best-attested event of the ancient world, beginning with the women whose grief on Friday became joy on Sunday.

sa.prompt: Explain the guards' report and the bribe, and why the lie actually testifies to the resurrection.
sa.model: Some of the guard came into the city and reported to the chief priests all that had happened, and the leaders gave the soldiers a large sum of money, telling them to say that the disciples came by night and stole the body while they slept. The soldiers took the money and spread that story among the Jews. Yet the lie actually testifies to the resurrection, because the enemies of Jesus did not deny that the tomb was empty and could not produce a body; they could only invent a poor story, since sleeping men make hopeless witnesses to a theft that supposedly happened while they slept. The very bribe they paid is a witness to the empty tomb they could not explain away.

sa.prompt: How does the resurrection defeat distress?
sa.model: The women came to the tomb in deep grief, carrying spices to do one last service for the Lord they loved, and they left running with great joy, for the resurrection turns sorrow into joy by answering our deepest distress, which is death itself. The author tells of his own first encounter with family grief as a boy, when his baby niece died after an operation and his mother cried, Why did God let our baby die. He admits he had no full answer then and has none now, yet he believes with all his heart that he will see her again because the tomb is empty and Christ is risen. So the resurrection does not pretend the grave is nothing, but it promises that the grave is not the end and that those who die in Christ will live again.

sa.prompt: How does the resurrection defeat doubt, in the story of Thomas?
sa.model: When Jesus first appeared in the upper room the disciples believed, but Thomas was absent and would not take their word, saying he would not believe unless he saw the nail scars and put his finger where the nails had been, for he knew dead men do not rise. A week later Jesus appeared again with Thomas present, showed him His hands and side, and Thomas answered, My Lord and my God. The author confesses that he too has had doubts, doubting whether there is a God, whether Christianity is true, whether God answers prayer and loves him, and whether he had the gifts to preach, and says that in the end it is the resurrection that conquers his doubts, for if Christ is risen then God is real and death is defeated. The Lord did not rebuke Thomas but met him in his doubt and turned it to worship.

sa.prompt: How does the resurrection defeat denial, in the restoration of Peter?
sa.model: Peter had sworn he would never fall away, yet within hours he denied his Lord three times, the last with cursing, but Jesus did not leave him to drown in guilt. On the seashore the risen Lord asked him three times whether he loved Him, one question for each denial, and three times gave him back his calling to feed His sheep, and the Peter who had denied Christ in a courtyard later stood up at Pentecost and preached Him boldly. The author confesses that he too has denied Christ, not as Peter did but in the subtler way of silence, staying quiet when God gave him an opening. The resurrection answers that failure, for the same Lord who restored Peter restores us, and the Spirit who emboldened a denier can embolden us to speak.

sa.prompt: How does the resurrection defeat disgust, in the conversion of Saul?
sa.model: Saul of Tarsus was filled with hatred for the church, going from house to house to drag off believers and imprison them, until on the road to Damascus a light from heaven flashed around him and he fell and heard a voice say, Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me, and when he asked who it was the answer came, I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting. The encounter with the risen Christ so transformed him that the great persecutor became the great missionary, and the man who had hunted Christians spent the rest of his life proclaiming Christ. So the resurrection can break even a heart set in hatred or turned away in bitterness, for the living Lord still meets people on their road and turns their disgust into worship.

sa.prompt: State the Great Commission and what it commands.
sa.model: Meeting the eleven on a mountain in Galilee, the risen Jesus declared that all authority in heaven and on earth had been given to Him, and on that authority commanded them to go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to observe all things He had commanded. The command is not merely to win converts but to make disciples, baptized into the triune name and taught to obey everything Christ commanded. So the Great Commission is the marching order of the whole church and not a suggestion for a gifted few, sending Christ's people to every nation under the authority of the risen King.

sa.prompt: Explain how Matthew's Gospel is framed by 'God with us' and 'I am with you always.'
sa.model: Matthew began his Gospel by saying the child would be called Immanuel, which means God with us, and he ends it with the risen Lord's promise, I am with you always, even to the end of the age, so that the whole book is framed and held between those two phrases. The God who came to be with us in a manger, who was with us through the teaching and the miracles, and who was with us even into the darkness of the cross, is now with us as the risen and reigning King and will be with us until the age is ended. This frame shows that the presence of God with His people is the great theme of the Gospel, and that the promise made at the beginning is sealed at the end by a Lord who has conquered death and will never leave us.

sa.prompt: Pull the unit together: what does the resurrection do, and what is our response?
sa.model: The resurrection changes lives, for Jesus is alive, He rose from the dead, and we are His witnesses. It removes our distress by promising that the grave is not the end, removes our doubt as it conquered Thomas, removes our denial as it restored Peter, and removes our disgust as it transformed Saul. Our response is to be His witnesses and to obey the Great Commission, going under the authority of a living King who has promised to be with us always. Every other grave in history has only footsteps leading in, but the tomb of Jesus has footsteps leading out, and because He lives, all who are in Christ shall live also, sent out in the joy and hope of the empty tomb.
